key_points.description: Meeting objective: demo Informatica's IDMC platform to Falcon's team, focusing on data cleanliness, deduplication, and data quality improvements for their Salesforce instance.

Current pain points confirmed: duplicate and incomplete account/company records, invalid candidate emails, incomplete candidate profiles limiting lead matching, and no scalable data remediation process — all impacting go-to-market effectiveness.

Data profiling was demonstrated first, showing how IDMC's Claire AI scans ingested data, flags anomalies (special characters, duplicate spellings, missing fields), and surfaces insights in natural language — schedulable with email alerts.
Standardization rules and dictionaries can be built to normalize inconsistent field values (e.g., product/policy type variants) and reused enterprise-wide across sources.

IDMC connects to virtually any modern tech stack — Snowflake, S3, REST APIs, JDBC/ODBC, flat files, FTP — with a drag-and-drop mapping interface that also supports natural language expression building.
Out-of-the-box address and email verification assets were highlighted; email verification performs a soft check for validity without pinging the internet directly.

Deduplication asset uses configurable matching strategies (e.g., name + email, name + company), fuzzy logic via Claire AI, cluster IDs for grouping duplicates, and survivorship rules to produce a single golden record.
Falcon's primary data issues center on unreachable candidates due to bad emails and missed candidate matches caused by inconsistent location coding and duplicate work history records in Salesforce.

Data flows primarily from LinkedIn into Salesforce via Krisp (automated enrichment ~1 day post-record creation) and a browser-based scraping tool; enrichment is manually triggered by staff who then review and continue with the candidate.
Kailash confirmed the desired workflow: post-enrichment, run data validation, deduplication, email verification, and golden record merging — batch rather than real-time.
Bulk uploads do not require real-time processing; a nightly batch for most records and a weekly schedule for others was agreed as the preferred approach.

Falcon's Salesforce instance holds approximately 75K contacts; the team acknowledged it is SMB-scale, and Informatica confirmed pricing and capacity have been tailored for the growth/SMB segment since the Salesforce acquisition.

Scoping inputs required from Falcon: total record volume and new record cadence (daily/weekly/monthly), data structure (Salesforce-only vs. flat files), email verification needs, and whether any historical data profiling or deduplication is needed — address verification confirmed as low priority.
